findings.text: The new test `Servex/agents/item-read-no-write.test.mjs` is listed only in `core/Session/doc/identity.md:56`; the item tool's own test list (`Servex/doc/item-tool.md:55`) and `Servex/agents/readme.md` don't mention it, so someone looking at the item tool won't find it. Add it to item-tool.md:55 next to `page_tools.test.mjs`.

The task folder holds only `requirements.md` and `review/diff.patch`. There is no `task.jsonl`, no outcome and no evidence for the brief's own Check (opening `/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/cloud-voice-app-20261106/` gives no writing POST and no 500), and the folder is untracked in git. A fresh agent can't tell whether that Check was ever run or whether the work has landed. Log the Check's result and commit the folder.

Both asks are met in code. `session_file` takes `{create}`, `run_item_now` passes `create:false` for a read or a SESSION_QUERIES delta (`page_tools.js:1592`), and a non-uuid id is looked up by the scan and never created. `AICost.session_url` now asks `AISession.page_url` (`AICost.js:171`), and AISession is already imported. I ran both tests in the worktree: `item-read-no-write: 14 checks pass` and `page_tools: 44 checks passed`.

There is a simpler way: `is_read` at `page_tools.js:1592` is the same expression the session-record branch repeats at `page_tools.js:1601` (`delta === undefined || …every(k => SESSION_QUERIES.includes(k))`). Line 1601 could use `is_read` (it also checks `Object.keys(delta).length`, so the two behave the same).

"A read never writes" is broader than what was built. A `summary` query on an older folder with no `session.jsonl` still writes a one-line record (`page_tools.js` just after 1601; documented in `core/Session/readme.md:133`). That is deliberate and creates no folder, so requirement 1 holds. But the test only watches folder listings (sessions/ and today's day folders), not the files inside an existing session folder. The cloud-voice-app-20261106 folder already has a `session.jsonl`, so viewing it writes nothing.

Every read of an unknown non-uuid name sets `AISession.scanned = false` and rescans all sessions (`session_file`, the new `!UUID.test(uuid)` branch). Any typo'd or unknown route now pays for a full scan. A cheaper path would try `page_url` first and rescan only when it misses.

`AICost.session_url` is a cache key, and it now changes value once the index names the session (bare id before, dated url after). The list and the session page can therefore cache under two keys and ask twice, which goes against the comment at `AICost.js:169`. `ai/AITask/readme.md:21` also still calls it only "the cost-summary key" and doesn't say it is now the dated url.

The worktree `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/read-no-write` has 158 uncommitted `files.jsonl` changes, dated 05:46, before the commit. Clear them before merging so they don't get swept in. The change in `page_tools.js` also needs a Servex restart before the Check can pass on the live site.

findings.text: `named_day_folder` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:166`) is a new, private session-folder finder. agents.md says to find a session folder with `SessionFolders.at(store).of(id)` and never by building a path, and `core/Session/SessionFolders.mjs:17` exists because "five finders each had their own rule". `SessionFolders.of()` refuses a non-uuid (`SessionFolders.mjs:166`), so the simpler, single fix is to teach `SessionFolders` to find a non-uuid record (a day folder named exactly for the id, newest first) and have `session_file` call it. Then the AISession scan, the page and Servex all get the same answer from one place.

The lookup accepts any day folder whose name matches, including folders that are not sessions. In the worktree, a read of `/framework/ai/sessions/cards/` resolves to `2026/11/10/cards/page.jsonl` (`{"ok":false,"why":"no such path: id","here":["title","_pages"]}`), and `/sessions/spawned/` resolves the same way. It's read-only, so nothing is written, but item 1's version should accept only a folder that holds a session record (`session.jsonl` or `index.json` naming that id).

Both asks hold after the follow-up. I ran both tests in `worktrees/read-no-write-2`: `item-read-no-write: 16 checks pass` and `page_tools: 44 checks passed`. `/sessions/voice-app/` now answers `cloud-voice-app-20261110`, and an unknown name (`no-such-xyz`) gets a reason, not a throw. Dropping the full `AISession.scan()` rescan also answers the previous review's note 6.

The follow-up commits (`d59e373d7`, `742da30c9`) are still only on the `read-no-write-2` worktree branch. The brief's Check hasn't been re-run against them on the live site, which needs a merge and a Servex restart. The last `task.jsonl` log line says so, which is enough for a fresh agent to continue. Add the post-merge Check result to `task.jsonl`.

`requirements.md` (last line) still says the test has "14 checks"; it now has 16. The test's added `session-folders.json` filter (`item-read-no-write.test.mjs:15`) is explained in its comment. `core/Session/doc/identity.md:56` and `Servex/doc/item-tool.md:55` are current. If item 1 is done, identity.md should name `SessionFolders` instead of `named_day_folder`.
